pageData.heading: Buying a Property Through Resale or Direct Purchase
pageData.para:
When it comes to buying a home most buyers opt for one of two preferred methods:
  • Resale Transactions (pre-owned properties)
  • Direct Purchase from Builders (new properties)
These methods cater to the diverse needs of homebuyers and involve different processes and costs. Here’s a quick overview to help you navigate these types of property purchases.

contents.heading: Resale Transactions
contents.para: A resale transaction refers to buying a property from an individual owner rather than directly from the builder.
contents.secPara:
Why Choose Resale Transactions?

Immediate Possession

Especially with registered properties, you can move in or rent them out right away.

Negotiation Opportunities

Prices are usually negotiable based on the property's condition and market value.

Well-Developed Infrastructure

These properties are often in established neighborhoods with existing amenities.

These properties can be:

  • Under construction: Unregistered but in the resale market, where the original buyer wishes to transfer ownership before possession.
  • Registered properties: Pre-owned properties where the sale deed is already executed, and ownership is legally transferred.

contents.heading: Direct Purchase from Builders
contents.para: A direct purchase involves buying a fresh, newly constructed property directly from a developer or builder. These properties are often in new residential projects or township developments.

list.heading: Customization Options:
list.desc: Buyers can select layouts, finishes, or even floors in under-construction properties.

list.heading: No Previous Ownership:
list.desc: You’ll be the first owner, and everything from fittings to interiors will be brand new.

list.heading: Builder Discounts & Offers:
list.desc: Builders often provide festival discounts, subvention schemes, or reduced interest rates.

contents.heading: Key Considerations for Buyers
contents.listTopPara: Whether you're buying through resale or directly from a builder, keep these factors in mind:

list.heading: Property Registration Status:
list.desc: Ensure the property is either registered or has clear ownership documents.

list.heading: Legal Due Diligence:
list.desc: Verify the title deed, encumbrance certificate, and applicable approvals.

list.heading: Stamp Duty & Registration Charges:
list.desc: Factor in these costs for registered properties.

list.heading: Builder Reputation:
list.desc: When purchasing directly, research the builder's past projects, delivery timelines, and reviews.

contents.heading: What Works for You?
contents.secPara:
Making the Right Choice:

  • If you want immediate possession or a property in an established locality, a resale transaction may be the better choice.

  • If you’re looking for new construction, customization options, or modern amenities, a direct purchase from a builder is ideal.

By understanding the nuances of these transaction types, you can make a more informed decision on your journey to becoming a homeowner.
